\clearpage\subsection{Comparison with other aligners}\label{sec:external-aligner-results}
The following adjustments were needed to run the compared aligners:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Minimap2.} A single FASTA record must fit within its signed 32-bit coordinate limit. We therefore split the 4 Gbp reference into two records of roughly 2 Gbp each. Returned positions are converted back to coordinates in the original reference. The 2 Gbp reference remains one record.
\item \textbf{Winnowmap.} We re-enabled saving its native index and changed loading to rebuild the weighting Bloom filter from the saved list of frequent k-mers produced by Meryl. We also initialized a repeat-length variable that otherwise produced undefined MAPQ values. The 4 Gbp references used index batches of 1,999 million bases. Where memory was still insufficient, we split the reference into 250 Mb records, overlapping by the longest query plus 64 bases, and reduced index batches to 499 million bases. Results from the index parts are merged, which can affect MAPQ.
\item \textbf{blastn.} We disabled low-complexity masking and required at least 80\% query coverage to remove short chance matches. Scoring uses match reward 2, mismatch penalty 4 and gap open/extension penalties 4/2, matching the first affine-gap branch of minimap2. BLAST has no second branch and scores N as $-3$ rather than $-1$. The default E-value threshold of 10 is retained.
\item \textbf{LexicMap.} Its 28-bit coordinates require records of at most 268,435,455 bases. We split the reference accordingly, with overlap equal to the longest query, and restore original coordinates in the results. On machines with less than 10 GiB RAM, the 4 Gbp reference was indexed one record per batch. We kept its native 20,000 LexicHash masks and alignment scoring. Query coverage is at least 80\%. Its reference encoding replaces N with A, while query bases are unchanged.
\end{itemize}
